summary:
Only a left-moving comet can crash, and the first thing it meets is the nearest survivor to its left, if that
one moves right. Keep survivors on a stack: a left-mover pops smaller right-movers off the top, stops at a bigger
one (and breaks), or ties (both go). O(n): every comet is pushed and popped at most once.

question.md:
Comets are listed in order of position. The sign is the direction (positive → right, negative → left), the
absolute value is the size. All fly at the same speed. When two meet, the smaller breaks; equal sizes both
break. Return the survivors, still in position order.

- **Only a → followed (somewhere to its right) by a ← can meet.** Two comets moving the same way keep their gap
  forever, and ← … → move apart.
- **One comet can win many collisions:** a big ← sweeps up several smaller → in a row.
- **Up to 10⁵ comets.**

think.md:
Take `[5, 10, -5, 8, -12, 3, -3, -1]`. The `−5` meets the `10` first and breaks. The `−12` meets `8`, then `10`, then `5`, winning
each time, so it survives and flies off to the left. `3` and `−3` destroy each other. `−1` has only `−12` to its
left, which flies the same way. Survivors: `[-12, -1]`.

Look at it from a ← comet's point of view. Everything to its left has already settled among itself: it's some
←s (flying away) followed by some →s (waiting to meet it). The nearest one is the first it will hit. If it wins,
the next nearest is next. That's always the **most recent survivor**, the top of a stack. A → comet just joins
the stack: nothing to its left can hit it, and whatever comes from the right will deal with it later.

approaches.title: Resolve one collision at a time

idea.md: Collisions only ever happen between neighbours facing each other (→ immediately followed by ←). Find the first such pair, remove the loser (or both), and scan again. When a full scan finds none, everything left survives.

build: Copy the comets into a list.
Loop: find the first index with `a[i] > 0 and a[i+1] < 0`; if none, stop.
Remove the smaller one (both if equal) and repeat.

lines.text: Work on a copy we can delete from.
Walk left to right looking for a collision.
Neighbours facing each other: the left one flies right, the right one flies left.
The smaller breaks; equal sizes both break.

notes.c: `removeAt` shifts the tail left over the removed comets.

lines.text: Removing comets can create a new facing pair further left, so scan from the start again.
No facing neighbours remain: these are the survivors.

complexity.md: **Time O(n²):** up to n collisions, and each costs a rescan plus a deletion that shifts the list. **Space O(n)** for the copy.

steps.text: Start. Positive comets fly right (→), negative ones fly left (←).
First facing pair at positions 1,2: 10 beats 5. Rescan from the start.
First facing pair at positions 2,3: 12 beats 8. Rescan from the start.
First facing pair at positions 1,2: 12 beats 10. Rescan from the start.
First facing pair at positions 0,1: 12 beats 5. Rescan from the start.
First facing pair at positions 1,2: both size 3: both break. Rescan from the start.
No pair faces each other any more: these survive.

walk.title: Find the first neighbouring pair that faces each other (→ then ←), resolve that one collision, and start scanning again.

limits.md: Each collision restarts the scan and shifts the array, so 10⁵ comets can take ~10¹⁰ steps. But a collision only ever involves the newest survivor to the left, so nothing needs rescanning: a stack keeps exactly the comets still in play.

approaches.title: Stack of survivors

idea.md: Go left to right with a stack of survivors so far. A → comet (or a ← with nothing to hit) is pushed. A ← comet of size `s` fights the top while the top is →: a smaller top is popped and the fight continues; an equal top is popped and `s` breaks too; a bigger top survives and `s` breaks. If `s` clears every → it meets, push it.

build: While alive, the comet moves left, and the top moves right: compare sizes and pop/kill as described.
The stack, bottom to top, is the answer.

lines.text: Survivors so far, in position order.

notes.java: An array with a `top` counter is the stack.
notes.c: An array with a `top` counter is the stack.

lines.text: A fight happens only when the incoming comet flies left and the nearest survivor flies right.
The top is smaller: it breaks, and the incoming comet goes on to meet the next one.
The top is bigger: the incoming comet breaks, and the top stays.
Still alive (it flies right, or it flies left with nothing left to hit): it's a survivor for now.
The stack, bottom to top, is in position order.

complexity.md: **Time O(n):** each comet is pushed at most once and popped at most once, so the inner loop runs O(n) times in total. **Space O(n)** for the stack.

steps.text: 5→: moves right: it can't hit anything to its left. Push.
10→: moves right: it can't hit anything to its left. Push.
8→: moves right: it can't hit anything to its left. Push.
←12 meets 8→: 12 > 8, the top breaks. Pop and keep going.
←12 meets 10→: 12 > 10, the top breaks. Pop and keep going.
←12 meets 5→: 12 > 5, the top breaks. Pop and keep going.
←12 cleared everything moving right; nothing left to hit. Push.
3→: moves right: it can't hit anything to its left. Push.
←1: the top also moves left; they never meet. Push.
The stack, bottom to top, is the answer: [-12, -1].

walk.title: Survivors so far sit on a stack. Only a left-mover can hit anything, and the first thing it meets is the stack's top.

takeaways.md:
- When each new item only interacts with **the most recent survivors**, keep the survivors on a stack.
- Amortised O(n): the inner `while` can run many times for one item, but every pop removes something for good.
- Spell out which pairs can interact at all (here only → … ←) before simulating.
